These observations open a new window on the stellar mass function and provide stringent tests of stellar models in the very low–mass regime (see Gerasimov et al. 2024; Ventura et al. 2026, for models of very low-mass stars in NGC 104). 

_• Metallicity distribution of first-population stars._ Studies of RGB stars have shown that 1P stars in most GCs exhibit extended sequences in ChM (Milone et al. 2015, 2018; Legnardi et al. 2022), reflecting small star-to-star metallicity variations (Marino et al. 2019a, 2023; Legnardi et al. 2022). More recently, a similar feature has been identified among M dwarfs in NGC 104 (Legnardi et al. 2024). The infrared dataset presented in this paper, when combined with optical _HST_ data, will allow us to constrain the metallicity distribution of lowmass stars with a precision of a few hundredths of a dex.[7] providing insight into the chemical properties of the primordial gas from which 1P stars formed. 

_• Mass functions of multiple populations._ Determining the luminosity and mass functions of GC stars, including their distinct populations, is crucial for understanding cluster formation and evolution. In particular, comparing the MFs of 1P and 2P stars provides constraints on the possible dependence of the initial mass function (IMF) on the formation environment. If 2P stars formed under significantly denser conditions than 1P stars, differences in their present-day MFs may reveal whether the IMF is universal or varies with environment (Dondoglio et al. 2022).

## 6. CONCLUSIONS 

PNe that are physically associated with star clusters are scarce, though important for stellar evolution studies. In this work, we used CS and cluster published catalogues along with Gaia data in an attempt to uncover more of such rare occurrences. We initially uncovered 38 CS-cluster pairs whose kinematic and positional data cannot exclude a possible association (see Table 1). There are 46 additional pairs whose components’ angular proximity suggests a possible association but which lack kinematic CS Gaia data. Since these associations cannot be properly explored with the available data, they are presented separately in Table C1 of the Appendix. Our kinematically consistent candidate pairs were then further explored in terms of interstellar extinction compatibility and consistency with evolutionary models and predictions (see Table 3). Based on the available data and our complete analysis, we find that seven pairs in our sample pass all of our kinematic, extinction, and evolutionary selection criteria, and thus have a higher likelihood of being true associations. Two of these associations are already confirmed or reported in the literature. We explore these seven associations separately, along with the questionable GJJC 1 

- NGC 6656 pair, finding that the PN PHRJ1855-0116 - OC UBC 1049 pair is our best candidate for followup. The initial and final masses of our best candidates generally agree with the latest IFMR estimates, as well as the points corresponding to confirmed or reported cluster-PNe (see Figure 2). 

The source catalogues, which serve as the basis of this work, are not complete (e.g., E. L. Hunt & S. Reffert 2023), and thus more possible pairs could remain hidden from the current study. More data are needed to explore the reported candidate CS-cluster associations. Some of the clusters and CSs in our sample are themselves candidates, so they must first be confirmed. Improved precision in the estimation of cluster, PN and CS kinematic and physical parameters is also required in many cases. questions.question: According to the paper "Dust destruction in bubbles driven by multiple supernovae explosions", how does the total mass of interstellar dust destroyed by clustered (multiple) SNe compare to the mass destroyed by the same number of isolated SNe, and what quantitative implication does this have for the dust lifetime in the ISM?
questions.reference_answer: The paper finds that the mass of dust destroyed by multiple SNe in clusters is approximately 10% of that destroyed by an ensemble of the same number of isolated SNe. Consequently, the lifetime of dust in the ISM is longer by about a factor of ≃10 compared to values previously derived assuming isolated SNe. (evidence: evidence_id 942c7ece2b94197a492ae517)
questions.support_summary: The paper reports that (1) the mass of dust destroyed in a multi-SNe bubble saturates after a certain epoch and the saturation timescale is proportional to the SN rate; (2) the dust mass destroyed per SN decreases for higher SN rate and the destruction efficiency in homogeneous-media bubbles drops for higher-mass clusters (e.g., around clusters with mass ≳4×10^4 M☉ it is <0.4%); and (3) multiple-SNe in clusters destroy approximately 10% of the dust mass compared to the same number of isolated SNe, implying dust lifetime in the ISM is longer by a factor ≃10 than previous isolated-SN estimates. (evidence: evidence_id 942c7ece2b94197a492ae517).

reference_evidence.text:
## **5. Conclusion** 

We have considered the destruction of dust in shells driven by multiple SNe explosions in stellar clusters. Using 3D hydrodynamic simulations, we have investigated how the single-size interstellar dust grains are destroyed in the multiSNe bubble expanding in a homogeneous as well as clumpy medium. Our results can be summarized as follows: 

- The mass of dust destroyed in the multi-SNe bubble does not grow after a certain epoch and becomes saturated, while SNe continue to explode. The timescale for this saturation is proportional to SNe rate in cluster; 

- The mass of dust destroyed in bubble per SN decreases for higher SN rate; the destruction efficiency – the ratio of the the total mass of dust destroyed by clustered SNe to the value of dust destroyed by the same number of isolated SNe – in bubbles evolving in a homogeneous medium drops for higher mass clusters. E.g., around clusters with _𝑀_ ∗ ∼4 _>_ × 104 _𝑀⊙_ , it is less 0.4%. For lower mass clusters the efficiency is proportional to Δ _𝑡_ ∕ _𝑡𝑙𝑓,𝑚𝑎𝑥_ . Therefore, the destruction of the interstellar dust is controlled by SNe in lowmass clusters. 

- The mass of dust destroyed by multiple SNe in clusters approximately 10% of that in an ensemble of equal number of isolated SN. Thus, the lifetime of dust in the ISM is longer by a factor ∼10 compared to the value previously derived in the literature for isolated SN. 

- In a clumpy medium the efficiency increases by about a factor of 1 _._ 5 in bubbles formed around clusters with _𝑀_ ∗ ∼4 × 10[4] _𝑀⊙_ and up to 4 times around _𝑀_ ∗ ∼ 8 × 10[5] _𝑀⊙_ .

## **6 DISCUSSION** 

Our NGC 1901 sample of benchmark stars includes F, G, and early K-type dwarfs and spans the _𝑇_ eff range 4100–6200 K, corresponding to the colour range 0.66≤( _𝐺_ BP − _𝐺_ RP)0 ≤1.7. Hotter stars have a shallower convection zone, responsible for a less efficient angular momentum loss compared to cooler stars with deeper convective envelopes (Barnes 2010). After rejecting fast rotators and outliers, most of our 32 benchmark stars line up on a common slow-rotator sequence (see Fig. 9). The sequence follows the expected morphology: cooler, lower mass stars exhibit longer rotation periods, with a turnover to a more rapid rotation near 5800 K. 

The empirical framework used to model rotational evolution yielded the age value _𝜏_ gyro-interp = 830 ± 50 Myr. While this is slightly younger than the isochronal age of 890 Myr derived by Cantat-Gaudin et al. (2020), it is consistent within _<_ 2 _𝜎_ . Our PARSEC v1.2S isochrones provide the best match to the observed cluster distribution, at the rotational age _𝜏_ gyro-interp (black line in Fig. 2). 

For stars hotter than 5900 K, the rotation sequence of NGC 1901 overlaps with the reference benchmark clusters. However, for late G and K-type dwarfs, our distribution of rotation periods becomes flatter and diverges from them. Our magnitude and membership cuts limited the sample to stars cooler than ∼4100 K (K7 spectral type). Stars at the cooler end of the CMD are also faint, hindering a robust detection of a rotational signal, namely the rotation sequence can become noisy and the scatter in the measured _𝑃_ rot is likely to increase. We note that even after careful membership and rotational analyses, rotational outliers are common in star clusters, as shown in the literature (e.g. Godoy-Rivera et al. 2021). questions.question: Comparing the two papers 'The Ashes of Supermassive Stars: Globular Cluster-like Aluminum Enhancement in Little Red Dots' and 'SPURS: An Ultra-deep View Inside the Compact, Nitrogen-Enriched Nuclei of Little Red Dots': do the spectral signatures reported indicate that (a) the aluminum-rich, magnesium-poor blueshifted absorbing gas identified in the LRD stacked spectrum is kinematically consistent with the broad, high-velocity [O III] emission components seen in individual LRDs, and (b) can the excerpts support a conclusion that both phenomena arise from the same high-velocity outflow around the central engine?
questions.reference_answer: No. The excerpts show (a) the stacked LRD spectrum exhibits blueshifted absorption in Al III and other absorption features at ~-140 km s^-1 relative to systemic, indicating aluminum-rich, magnesium-poor gas around the central engine (evidence_id: bcb075d7546ed4fd57924643). (b) The SPURS paper reports broad [O III] emission components in individual LRDs with FWHM = 1130–1627 km s^-1, and that models including broad components are strongly preferred (evidence_id: 07507c678ea7f30347e2e8bd). These two kinematic measurements are incompatible: the absorption is at ~-140 km s^-1 while the broad [O III] components have characteristic widths of >1000 km s^-1. The provided excerpts do not present any evidence tying the ~-140 km s^-1 absorption component to the >1000 km s^-1 [O III] emission (no overlapping velocities, no statement of a common origin), so they do not support a conclusion that both phenomena arise from the same high-velocity outflow around the central engine (evidence_ids: bcb075d7546ed4fd57924643; 07507c678ea7f30347e2e8bd).

Paper 'SPURS: An Ultra-deep View Inside the Compact, Nitrogen-Enriched Nuclei of Little Red Dots' reports detection of broad [O III] components (FWHM = 1130–1627 km/s) in four LRDs, with fits preferring models including broad components (evidence_id: 07507c678ea7f30347e2e8bd).

questions.question: Comparing the two studies — 'Tidal origin of dark-matter free dwarf galaxies in the NGC 1052 group' and 'A new clump-based star formation model for galaxy simulations: implications for high-redshift compact star clusters' — do the simulated tidal dwarf galaxies (TDGs) produced in the NGC 1052 major-merger models have the internal properties (stellar mass scale, surface brightness/extension, and likelihood of forming dense bound star clusters) expected from the clump-driven, high-efficiency star formation in compact discs reported by the CSF model paper?
questions.reference_answer: No. The NGC 1052 merger models produce TDGs that are described as faint, extended, and low surface brightness and can reach stellar masses up to ~3×10^9 M☉ in favorable cases (evidence: 04c7fdc48bc7db7d6d3415c7, 1080978cacdd4f1923864231). By contrast, the CSF model indicates that formation of dense, bound star clusters and very high local star-formation efficiencies occurs in compact galactic discs that generate very dense clumps (e.g., maximum clump masses up to ~10^7 M☉ and clump surface densities >10^4 M☉ pc^-2 in the 10^10 M☉ halo runs, with bound cluster mass fractions of ~10–70% only for sufficiently high compactness; evidence: 0c3dbf13da9dd4027969933c, 9ee13cd7e925ed789689fa3d, 160dd9270d4a618cf6df643a). The TDGs from the NGC 1052 models are low-surface-brightness, extended objects rather than the compact, cluster-rich systems that the CSF paper associates with high compactness and clump-driven high-efficiency star formation. Therefore, based on the excerpts, the TDGs in the NGC 1052 simulations do not share the compact, cluster-dominated internal structure that the CSF model predicts for systems formed via extreme clump-driven star formation in compact discs (citations: 04c7fdc48bc7db7d6d3415c7; 1080978cacdd4f1923864231; 0c3dbf13da9dd4027969933c; 9ee13cd7e925ed789689fa3d; 160dd9270d4a618cf6df643a).
questions.support_summary: Fouquet et al. (this paper: 'Tidal origin of dark-matter free dwarf galaxies in the NGC 1052 group') find that a major merger of NGC 1052 can produce tidal tails and TDGs whose stellar masses can reach ~3×10^9 M☉ and that TDGs produced in their modelling are faint, extended, and low surface brightness. The CSF model paper ('A new clump-based star formation model for galaxy simulations: implications for high-redshift compact star clusters') finds that compact discs produce dense, massive gas clumps (maximum clump mass up to ~10^7 M☉ in 10^10 M☉ halos) and that bound cluster mass fractions can reach ~10–70% depending on compactness and halo mass; self-gravitationally bound star clusters form only in sufficiently compact discs (_>=8 in some runs).

reference_evidence.text:
## **5. Conclusions** 

In this work, we have verified that a major merger experienced by NGC 1052 produces tidal tails and TDGs that match the intrinsic properties of DM-deficient dwarfs discovered by van Dokkum et al. (2018, 2019) as well as their alignment along a trail. Our finding results from simple adaptations of the N- body hydrodynamical simulations made by Wang et al. (2020) to reproduce the properties of Cen A, and we addressed the supposed failures of the TDG scenario. The only limitation of our - modelling comes from its very large parameter space and insuffi ciently precise constraints on NGC 1052 and associated dwarfs, which prevented us from experimenting with a more accurate reproduction of the observations. 

According to the hierarchical scenario, the present-day E4 morphology of NGC 1052 takes its origin from its last major merger, which requires radial orbits, moderate gas fraction, a mass ratio close to 1:1, and specific orientations of the progenitor galaxies (Wang et al. 2020). The latter conditions are necessary to remove most of the angular momentum in the remnant, which is currently accompanied by large tidal tails and TDGs and match better the observations when compared to the bulletdwarf scenario. 

The bullet-dwarf scenario suffers from two major difficulties: first, reproducing the dwarf progenitors and, second, providing far too compact DM-deficient dwarfs. The scenario also neglects the fact that NGC 1052 is an active nucleus E4 galaxy showing tides, and it has likely experienced a major merger that can produce TDGs resembling the observed DM-deficient dwarfs. The likely occurrence of massive galaxy mergers near NGC 1052 has to be compared to the very rare dwarf–dwarf collision events in the field, for which only ten have been found in a (100Mpc)[3] volume from _z_ =3 to _z_ =0 (Lee et al. 2024). Future observations of dwarf radial distances will probe which of the two scenarios is the most likely. The dwarf GC over-luminosity appears to support the bullet-dwarf scenario, though there might be subtle selection effects associated with this property.

The estimated 3D distance of 1.7±0.5 Mpc between DF2 and DF4 (Shen et al. 2023) would mean that the trail of dwarfs extends almost exclusively along the line of sight. This estimate is essential for the bullet-dwarf scenario because it is the only way to account for an ancient-dwarf collision consistent with the DF2 age, while it could be fatal for the TDG scenario, which predicts a tidal tail elongated along all directions but limited to ∼ 1 Mpc in length. During the refereeing process, a new study by Tang et al. reference_evidence.text:
## **5 CONCLUSION** 

We have investigated how the compactness of galactic discs regulates clumpy star formation and the formation of bound star clusters. To this end, we have developed a new star formation model (CSF) in which star-forming gas clumps are identified on-the-fly and converted into stars with an efficiency _𝜖_ SF set by the clump surface density Σc, calibrated against the radiation hydrodynamics simulations of Fukushima & Yajima (2021). We apply the model to isolated disc galaxies embedded in haloes of _𝑀_ h = 10[9] , 10[10] and 10[11] M⊙ with a fixed gas-to-halo mass ratio of 0 _._ 01, adopting disc scale radii 

appropriate for _𝑧_ = 0–10 as a proxy for compactness. Our main results are summarised as follows. 

(i) Compact discs form more massive and denser gas clumps. In the 10[10] M⊙ haloes, the maximum clump mass increases from ∼ 10[5] _[.]_[1] to 10[7] _[.]_[4] M⊙ and the maximum clump surface density from ∼ 10[2] _[.]_[9] to _>_ 10[4] _[.]_[0] M⊙ pc[−][2] between _𝑧_ = 0 and 10. The fraction of clumps exceeding Σc _,_ th = 300 M⊙ pc[−][2] rises from 0 _._ 25 at _𝑧_ = 0 to 0 _._ 34 at _𝑧_ = 6 and 0 _._ 38 at _𝑧_ = 10, and the most compact discs host clumps with _𝜖_ SF ∼ 1.

(ii) This shift in clump properties translates directly into more efficient and burstier galactic star formation. In the 10[10] M⊙ haloes, the global SFE at _𝑡_ = 3 _𝑡_ dyn increases monotonically from 5 × 10[−][3] at _𝑧_ = 0 to 2 × 10[−][1] at _𝑧_ = 10, with peak SFRs of ∼ 1 M⊙ yr[−][1] reached before _𝑡_ ≈ _𝑡_ dyn for _𝑧_ ≥ 6. Less compact discs instead form stars intermittently at 10[−][2] –10[−][1] M⊙ yr[−][1] . 

(iii) The accompanying feedback disrupts the gaseous discs of the most compact systems. The _𝑧_ ≥ 8 galaxies retain little gas near the centre by _𝑡_ = 3 _𝑡_ dyn, whereas the _𝑧_ ≤ 2 discs survive three rotations. Stellar spiral arms show the opposite trend, becoming progressively more prominent towards higher _𝑧_ , indicating that compact discs assemble dynamically coherent stellar structures on timescales of ∼ 100 Myr even while their gas is being expelled.

(iv) Self-gravitationally bound star clusters form only in compact discs. No bound clusters appear at _𝑧_ ≤ 2 in the 10[10] M⊙ haloes, whereas the bound cluster mass fraction reaches ≈ 40 per cent at _𝑧_ ≥ 8. The threshold compactness depends on halo mass. In the 10[9] M⊙ haloes only the _𝑧_ = 10 run forms bound clusters, while in the 10[11] M⊙ haloes every run does, with fractions rising from ≈ 10 per cent at _𝑧_ = 0 to ≈ 70 per cent at _𝑧_ = 10. Halo mass therefore acts alongside compactness in regulating bound cluster formation, and the global SFE spans 2 × 10[−][3] –5 × 10[−][2] , 5 × 10[−][3] –2 × 10[−][1] and 2 × 10[−][2] –4 × 10[−][1] for _𝑀_ h = 10[9] , 10[10] and 10[11] M⊙, respectively. 

(v) The choice of star formation prescription is itself a leading factor. In the 10[10] M⊙ haloes, the KS runs retain their gas discs at all redshifts, show no strongly bursty histories, reach peak SFRs an order of magnitude below the CSF runs at _𝑧_ = 10, and saturate at SFE ≈ 5 × 10[−][2] for _𝑧_ ≥ 6 instead of continuing to rise with compactness. The resulting global SFEs are lower than in the CSF runs by factors of a few.

questions.question: Comparing the two studies 'A Homogenized Catalogue of Variable Stars in the Globular Cluster M22: Membership, Physical Parameters, and Distance' and 'Unresolved triple systems in the aged open cluster Trumpler 19: Discovery, confirmation, and implications', which cluster is more metal-poor, which cluster is closer to the Sun, and which cluster shows a higher fraction of unresolved higher-order (triple or greater) stellar systems according to the reported measurements?
questions.reference_answer: M22 is the more metal-poor cluster: the RR Lyrae-based metallicity for M22 is [Fe/H] = -1.73 ± 0.17 dex (evidence_id: 8899fe5bed8a3bb6570dd8c1). Trumpler 19 is farther from the Sun than the comparisons given for M22: M22's distance is D = 3.27 ± 0.14 kpc (evidence_id: 8899fe5bed8a3bb6570dd8c1), while Trumpler 19 is reported at d = 2.3 kpc (evidence_id: 1128d8621ff68fdf6e67654b). Therefore, Trumpler 19 is closer to the Sun than M22. Trumpler 19 shows the higher fraction of unresolved higher-order systems: its unresolved triple+higher-order fraction is THF = 0.084 ± 0.010, which is larger than the quoted THF for the open cluster M67 (0.029 ± 0.010); M22 has no reported THF in the provided excerpts (evidence_ids: 1128d8621ff68fdf6e67654b, 8c7b6a72fd7d4c8cfc22d71c).
questions.support_summary: Paper 'A Homogenized Catalogue of Variable Stars in the Globular Cluster M22: Membership, Physical Parameters, and Distance' reports a mean RR Lyrae-based metallicity [Fe/H] = -1.73 ± 0.17 dex and distance D = 3.27 ± 0.14 kpc for M22, and classifies M22 as Oosterhoff Type II with RRab mean period 0.65 ± 0.05 d. Paper 'Unresolved triple systems in the aged open cluster Trumpler 19: Discovery, confirmation, and implications' reports that Trumpler 19 has an unresolved triple+higher-order fraction THF = 0.084 ± 0.010, higher than M67's THF = 0.029 ± 0.010, and discusses multiplicity fractions compared with the solar neighborhood.

Somehow Trumpler 19 managed to create more multiple systems, or M 67 has more efficiently destroyed the multiple systems. Note that M 67 is an evolved cluster that has a comparable present mass of _M_ = 2000 _M_ ⊙ and that has lost most of its mass in the past (Hurley et al., 2005), similar to Trumpler 19, which has a present mass _M_ = 2400 _M_ ⊙ and which has also lost most of its mass (Sheikh et al., 2025).

It is well known that a large fraction of stars in the solar neighborhood appear in binary or higher-order systems (Duquennoy & Mayor, 1991). For example, (Tokovinin, 2014, 2023) found that the frequency of field multiple systems follows the distribution _N_ = 1 : 2 : 3 : 4 : 5, with relative numbers of _f_ = 54 : 33 : 8 : 4 : 1..This means that, on average, every 54 isolated stars there are 111 stars in multiple systems. This is in good agreement with the results from Raghavan et al. (2010) that reported 56% singles, 33% binaries, 8% triplets, and 3% higher multiplets. Also, more recently, the updated sample from Reyle et al. (2021) in the 10 pc solar neighborhood yields _N_ = 246 single stars, 69 binaries, 19 triples, 3 quadruples, and 2 quintuples (this means 339 objects in total that would be unresolved if placed at the distance of Trumpler 19). That yields 217 stars belonging to multiplets (47% of the total stars, or 64% of unresolved sources at 2.3 kpc). reference_evidence.text: There are triple systems known in open clusters that have been previously well characterized. We can cite a few specific examples such as M 67 (Sandquist et al., 2003), NGC2516 and NGC6530 (Gonzalez et al., 2014), NGC6819 (Brewer et al., 2016), and Ruprecht 147 (Torres et al., 2021). However, a sequence such as the one we observe here has never been reported. The comparison with the open cluster M 67 in particular is very interesting, because this cluster has a similar age ( _t_ = 4 Gyr), and metallicity ( _Z_ = 0), as Trumpler 19, and it is very well studied because it is located at _d_ = 900 pc, significantly closer than Trumpler 19, with _d_ = 2300 pc. The CMDs of M 67 (Leiner et al., 2025) show that there are a couple of stars in the region associated with triple and quadruple systems, but these do not form a sequence similar to the one we find in Trumpler 19. This indicates that the multiplicity fractions for these two clusters of a similar age are very different. We measure the unresolved triple and higher-order fraction as defined by Offner et al. (2023), finding that this fraction in Trumpler 19 (THF = 0.084 ± 0.010) is higher than that of the open cluster M 67 (THF = 0.029 ± 0.010). Therefore, there are nearly three times more unresolved triples and quadruples in Trumpler19 than in M 67. This fraction was measured within the color range 2.25 < _BP_ − _Ks_ < 4.75 mag for Trumpler 19, and 1.80 < _BP_ − _Ks_ < 4.30 mag for M 67, respectively (the color difference is due to the different mean cluster reddenings). This color range corresponds approximately to MS stars of spectral types roughly from G5V to M0V, temperatures from 3800 K to 5300 K, and masses within 0.5 < _M_ / _Mo_ < 0.9 (even though it is not straightforward to apply these parameters for our targets because they are composite systems).
